one_liner: VK's ahead-of-time compiler from strictly typed PHP to C++; first-party 5-7x over PHP 7.4 on Zend benchmarks.
what_it_does: KPHP analyzes a whole PHP project, infers a static type for every variable, translates it to C++ and compiles that into one Linux binary: by default a server with an embedded web server and process orchestration, or a CLI binary, or a static library plus header to link into C++ (--mode server|cli|lib, plus k2-* modes for the new light runtime). It accepts only a strictly typed subset of PHP, so it is not a drop-in replacement for php-fpm: the intended workflow is developing and testing on PHP, then compiling with KPHP for production.
how_it_is_fast: Whole-program type inference replaces PHP's dynamic zvals with concrete C++ types (ints, floats, strings, typed vectors), so arithmetic and array access compile to native code. All symbols are resolved at compile time: constants are inlined, getters and setters are inlined, class fields are fixed memory offsets instead of hashtable lookups, access modifiers vanish at runtime, and refcount flapping is reduced; the runtime adds constant-array pre-initialization and script allocators. The generated C++ is then built by g++ or clang (current default -O2); the gain largely disappears when types degrade to mixed.
when_to_use: Large PHP code bases with CPU-bound business logic that can be kept strictly typed and deployed as a Linux service; VK reports 2.7-10.6x faster page generation than PHP 7.2 (vk.com/feed 10.1 s vs 0.95 s).
Numeric or ML-style kernels over typed arrays: VK reports neural-network code at ~8 s vs 0.24 s and deep decision trees at ~5 s vs 0.14 s against PHP.
PHP-style code that calls C libraries heavily: KPHP's FFI passes internal pointers and skips CData casts, and with critical sections disabled approaches native call speed.
Teams that want whole-program compile errors and type, immutability and checked-exception checks before deploy, while still developing and testing on stock PHP.
Embedding PHP-subset business logic into a C++ program through lib mode (static library and header).
when_not_to_use: Existing code that relies on eval, reflection, dynamic names, generators, anonymous classes, finally, func_get_args, general references, SPL, XML/DOM, $_SESSION, image functions, file upload, Postgres/Redis clients or PHP extensions: none of these are supported, and the README warns existing code rarely compiles without rewriting.
Code dominated by built-in C functions such as strpos or parse_url: the benchmarks page itself says KPHP gains almost nothing there.

Allocation- and object-tree-heavy code: issue #541 (open since 2022-06-22, no maintainer reply) reports benchmarks-game binarytrees at 6.34 s user time on KPHP vs 1.94 s for PHP without JIT and 1.27 s with JIT.

Comparisons against modern PHP: every number is against PHP 7.4 or 7.2 without the opcache JIT (PHP 8.0+); the catalogue's php-src entry shows that JIT alone gives 2-9.5x on numeric kernels without any rewrite, so the remaining gap over PHP 8.x is not measured.

Windows hosts (Docker only) or systems without apt: deb packages are amd64-only for Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 and Debian 10/11, macOS needs a source build, and source builds have open failure reports (issue #1057, link error, open since 2024-08-05).

integration.form: compiler (PHP to C++ translator plus runtime library) producing a server or CLI binary, or a static lib plus header in lib mode
integration.dependencies: A C++ compiler at compile time (--cxx / KPHP_CXX); install via the vkcom/kphp Docker image or the kphp and vk-tl-tools deb packages from VK's artifactory; php7.4/8.x-vkext for developing on PHP; CMake 3.16+ for source builds
integration.min_toolchain: KPHP itself: C++17 with gcc 8.3+ or clang 10+; the k2 light runtime: C++23 with gcc 10.1+ or clang 14+. Generated code is compiled with the same -std as the KPHP build.
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 (generated code built with -march=sandybridge) and aarch64 (-march=armv8.2-a+crypto); macOS from source; no native Windows
integration.thread_safety: Not documented as a threading model for user code; PHP code keeps single-threaded semantics, concurrency comes from the embedded server's process orchestration and KPHP coroutines (forks), and data shared across requests uses a dedicated shared-memory API.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: compiles PHP source, but only a strictly typed subset without eval, reflection, generators, SPL or extensions; existing code usually needs rewriting, and a few behaviours differ (64-bit wrapping integer overflow, typed arrays returning non-null for missing keys)

gotchas: Build flags have changed since the docs were written: kphp2cpp.cpp now defaults the generated code's flags to '-O2 -ggdb -fsigned-char', and compiler-settings.cpp adds -fwrapv -fno-strict-aliasing -fno-omit-frame-pointer and -march=sandybridge on x86-64, while the walk-through still says KPHP builds with -Os. The doc's C++ comparison (-Os) and timings therefore do not describe current builds, and binaries will not run on x86-64 CPUs without AVX.

Harness: the walk-through's ~7x step (PHP ~1950 ms vs KPHP ~270 ms) gives KPHP its native array_swap_int_keys built-in while PHP runs a userland polyfill with two isset checks per swap (PHP slowed from ~2100 to ~2650 ms when switched to it), PHP is never given an inlined swap, and the input comes from unseeded rand(); the Zend runs used locally modified scripts that are not published, on unstated hardware.

Types that degrade to mixed erase most of the gain: the same quicksort fell from ~270 ms to ~940 ms once $argv made the array mixed[], and object field access pays null checks because nullability is not tracked.

Semantics differ from PHP in edge cases: integer overflow wraps as native 64-bit (compiled with -fwrapv) instead of becoming float, bitwise operators assume integers, and invalid-argument behaviour of standard functions differs.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: KPHP is the PHP counterpart of Codon, Shed Skin and mypyc (ahead-of-time compilers for a typed subset): pick it when the code base is PHP and you can accept rewriting to its typed subset for a 3-10x first-party gain. For unmodified PHP, PHP's own opcache JIT (php-src in this catalogue) needs no rewrite and on issue #541's binarytrees was faster than KPHP.
verified_claims_summary: First-party docs only: on php-src Zend micro_bench.php and bench.php (with a couple of tests removed and errors fixed, scripts not published), five runs each, PHP 7.4 with OpCache and no JIT averaged 3.297 s and 0.659 s vs KPHP 0.460 s and 0.119 s (about 7.2x and 5.5x, derived from page data), with no CPU, KPHP version or compiler stated. A quicksort walk-through reports ~2100 vs ~480 ms (~4x) and ~1950 vs ~270 ms after KPHP-specific tuning, and vk.com page timings vs PHP 7.2 show 2.7-10.6x.
status_note: Active (last commit 2026-09-25; recent work is mostly the new k2 light runtime) and usable via Docker or amd64 deb packages, but GPL-3.0 with no linking exception in LICENSE, so distributed binaries that link the runtime carry GPL obligations.
